newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola rises on commercials, Thunder Bay plug.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola rises on commercials, Thunder Bay plug.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial and commission house buying as oilseeds stockpiled in Thunder Bay awaiting vessels, traders said.

"There was commercial support in the November. Commission houses bought and locals sold at the close," a trader said. "Right now, we're waiting for a canola vessel," Manitoba Pool Elevators' operations general manager Dennis Hunter said. Nov-Jan spread at $4.30, Mar-July $2.50, Jan-Mar $3. November crush margin fell to -38.08. Volume was 3,300 lots.
November canola rose $0.20 to $399.30, January rose $1 to $404.40. November flax rose $4 to $369 on commercial demand.
Thunder Bay is the pricing point in the flax contract and MPE's Hunter said flax is to be loaded on a vessel soon.
November barley rose $1.30 to $146.30 on commission buying and active spreading. Nov-Feb spread $2.10. Oats didn't trade.
October feed wheat fell $0.60 at $176.90, December rose $1.10 to $169.30 on light hedges at the close, late commission buying. The contract's delivery point is Thunder Bay.
December feed peas fell US$1 to US$197 on commercials sales spurred on by lower CBOT soymeal values.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
